content.text:
I fixed it: Babel now keeps the parentheses around a function expression when it starts a statement that ends in `++` or `--`. Before, `(function(){})().map++;` came out as `function () {}().map++;`, which Node rejects with "Function statements require a function name". It now prints `(function () {})().map++;`.

**Cause:** the code generator decides whether a function at the start of a statement needs parentheses by walking up the expression to see whether it really is first. That walk handled calls, member access, assignments and similar cases, but it stopped at a postfix `++`/`--`. So it never reached the statement and dropped the parentheses.

**Fix:** in `packages/babel-generator/src/node/parentheses.ts`, the walk now also passes through postfix `++`/`--` (the `isFirstInContext` check, plus the matching `@babel/types` import). Prefix `++x` is left alone, because there the function isn't first anyway.

**Checks:** besides the issue's case, I tried `(function(){}).x--;`, `({}).x++;` and `(class{}).x++;`, and all keep their parentheses. The existing `babel-generator` tests pass (532 passed, 4 skipped). I didn't add a new test for this case.

The TypeScript "unused parameter" warnings in `parentheses.ts` are on lines I didn't touch.
